thread.title: Cuccinelli Defends Trump's Use of Alien Enemies Act
thread.title_full: Cuccinelli Defends Trump's Use of Alien Enemies Act

author: Jim Thomas
title: Cuccinelli Defends Trump's Use of Alien Enemies Act
text:
• Ken Cuccinelli, former acting Deputy Secretary of Homeland Security, defended President Trump's use of the 1798 Alien Enemies Act.
• Cuccinelli characterized the Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua as an arm of the Maduro regime.
• He stated that the courts have no role in reviewing the president's authority under the Alien Enemies Act.
• Cuccinelli claimed that Trump was correct to declare Tren de Aragua's presence in the U.S. as an invasion.
• The 1798 Alien Enemies Act allows the president to detain and deport nationals of hostile foreign powers during wartime or national emergencies.
• Cuccinelli emphasized that Tren de Aragua is different from other gangs like MS-13, as they are allegedly acting on behalf of the Venezuelan government.
• Trump's use of the Alien Enemies Act has faced legal challenges, with some deportations temporarily halted by judges.
• Cuccinelli expressed confidence that higher courts would uphold Trump's policy.
• The Justice Department requested to postpone a court-ordered disclosure of information on deportation flights, citing potential catastrophic consequences.
• Cuccinelli acknowledged that Trump's approach under the Alien Enemies Act eliminates due process for individuals classified under it.
• He predicted that higher courts would support the administration's actions as legal battles continue.
